findings.title: Guard the access metadata copied into the replacement against concurrent drift
findings.trigger: An ACL/xattr-only edit tightens MERGED after permissions::candidate copied access metadata but before move/install; bytes, identity, mtime, uid/gid and mode are unchanged.
findings.behavior: Snapshot guards do not retain ctime or bounded ACL/xattr metadata. Both the last guard at save.rs:156 and displaced comparison at182 accept the unchanged Stamp/bytes, and installed candidate matches its own earlier snapshot. Save can report success with stale copied ACL, undoing the concurrent policy tightening on the current result. Retaining old inode in recovery does not preserve the current result access policy.
findings.evidence: Owned Linux fixture changes named-user POSIX ACL read(4) to none(0) while mask/mode remains0640. All sampled guarded fields and source bytes remain equal; only ctime/ACL bytes change. Candidate retains old ACL. See acl-drift-reproducer.json. Application save outcome is inferred from immutable control flow; no injected app runtime/new compile claimed.
findings.recommendation: Capture a bounded access-metadata fingerprint/descriptor with the guarded source and revalidate it before move and on the displaced inode before install. Account for rename changing ctime rather than naively comparing ctime across rename. Add deterministic save_with BeforeMove/AfterMove ACL-only mutation regression proving refusal/current policy retention. Review equivalent Windows descriptor-only changes because deny-data-write sharing need not deny security changes.
